name: Granite
lore: Tiny crystals of quartz, feldspar, and mica give granite its speckled look.

name: Sandstone
lore: Sand grains compact and cement together to form sandstone.

name: Basalt
lore: Basalt forms when lava cools, often along the ocean floor.

name: Calcite
lore: Calcite is a major ingredient in limestone and can form clear crystals.

name: Agate
lore: Bands of chalcedony record layers of silica deposited in a cavity.

name: Opal
lore: Tiny silica spheres can split light into flashes of rainbow color.

name: Fluorite
lore: Fluorite often grows as cubes and some specimens glow under ultraviolet light.

name: Jasper
lore: Iron oxides can turn this opaque variety of quartz a deep rusty red.

name: Amethyst
lore: Amethyst is purple quartz and often lines the inside of geodes.

name: Sapphire
lore: Blue sapphire is a variety of corundum, a mineral nearly as hard as diamond.

name: Emerald
lore: Traces of chromium or vanadium give this variety of beryl its green color.

name: Pyrite
lore: Pyrite is iron sulfide, famous for its shiny gold color and cube-shaped crystals.

name: Obsidian
lore: Lava that cools too quickly to form large crystals can become obsidian.

name: Diamond
lore: Diamond is made of carbon atoms joined in an exceptionally hard crystal structure.

name: Garnet
lore: Garnet can form many-sided crystals as rocks change under heat and pressure.

name: Tourmaline
lore: Tourmaline can grow in long columns with contrasting bands of color.
